```md
### Design (setting aspect = env NX_ASPECT: unset / 16:9 = today exactly; 21:9, 32:9, auto, or a number)
- vk.cpp wide_factor(): F = aspect / (16/9), clamped 1..2, width rounded to 8 game px (21:9: 1280 -> 1680, F 1.3125).
- vk.cpp make_image: every 16:9 render target (flags 8, 2D, width*9 == height*16, width >= 64: scene, depth, post chain,
  window textures, minimap RT) gets w = width * F * scale; Image::sx = F. Shadow maps etc. keep their size.
- vk_replay.cpp draw: viewport / scissor x scaled by scale * sx (stretch over the width), so full-screen post passes, the
  scene and texelFetch passes line up (support-buffer render_scale stays uniform: game-space x simply runs to 1680).
  Copies (OP_COPY_TEX_TEX blit coords, buffer->image full-region check) x by sx.
- Hor+: names.txt cam_proj_update 0x57b02c (engine projection object: type +0xc0 0 = perspective, fov y +0xa0, aspect
  +0xa4, near / far +0xa8 / +0xac, dirty +0xc4); hle_sys.cpp hook sets aspect 16:9 -> 16:9 * F before the matrix is built
  (kept in the object: frustum culling widens too). Found via the 736-byte scene camera uniform (floats 56..71 P, 72..87
  P^-1, 88..103 VP; debug NX_CAM_LOG=n logs blocks, NX_CAM_FIND=frame scans guest memory for P00/P11 copies) + `watch`.
- UI: the game draws scene AND UI into one target and copies it into a window texture (nvnWindowInitialize textures,
  g_window_tex): that copy's source = g_ui_target. UI phase of a frame = after the FXAA draw (fxaa_frag), or the whole
  frame when no FXAA draw came for 3 frames (menus / title). Centred (viewport x + width * (F - 1) / 2, no stretch): draws
  into g_ui_target in the UI phase with 36-byte vertices (layout panes: triangle lists or 4-vertex strips) or 28-byte
  (text glyphs), except a 4-vertex pane spanning >= 1270 x 710 (fades: stretched). Full-screen passes after FXAA (24-byte
  strips -1..1) and the minimap's own 16:9 target stretch. Debug NX_UW_LOG=n NX_UW_FRAME=f logs UI-phase draws (vertices).
- Present (vk.cpp fit_blit, both present paths; FSR 1 output too): picture keeps its shape inside the window (black
  bars). This also fixes today's stretched 16:9 picture on 21:9 / 16:10 screens (16:9 screens: unchanged, < 1% = full).
- Verified (uw18, slot 20 5F, 21:9 at 720p): wide field, Itsuki correct proportions, HUD centred 16:9, minimap intact
  (private/uw_field_21x9.png). Commit 3e91658.
- More rules after uw18 (commit after 3e91658): bind_resources sets g_draw_picture when a fragment texture is a 16:9
  picture >= 640x360 that is not a widened target; a screen-size 4-vertex pane (36 / 28 / 20-byte vertices) is centred
  (16:9) when it samples such a picture (title illustration + logo, camp background movie: vs 009cf000, 20-byte quad),
  stretched otherwise (fades, flashes, screen copies). 20-byte vertices otherwise stretch. Text glyphs (28 bytes) centre.
  UI mask target bc936150 (R8, fmt 1) is widened and its draws stretch (minimap disc correct).
- Hor+ log (NX_ASPECT + "uw: camera" lines, first 40): camera 788951e0 fov 1.047 is re-set to 16:9 by the game every
  frame (hook re-widens it each time; fine). NX_UW_NOCAM=1 (debug) disables the hook.
```

`PLAN_SETUP_PRECOMPILE.md`:

```md
# Plan: first-run setup, all-shader precompile, no shipped game code

Written 2026-10-30 from a design talk with the user (no code changed, written while another
session was running). Read with NOTES.md "session 36" (pipeline recipes, prewarm, cache_seed).

## Goals (user)

1. No shader stutter from the very first minute, also in areas nobody has visited.
2. No need for anyone (user or dev) to do a full playthrough to build a cache seed.
3. Remove the legal risk: the release must not contain translated game code or data
   derived from the game.
4. Keep the Ryujinx MIT shader translator (user decision 10-30: do NOT write our own).

## Model: SavageWind (BotW/TotK recomp)

Their first-run screen: user picks the folder with their own extracted game (exact versions
listed), toggles "Precompile all shaders" (default On: "a few more minutes, ~1.5 GB", can be
done later from the config app), then "Set up game files". The download holds only tools; the
game code is built and every shader translated on the user's PC.

## Why the release is risky today

- `tms.exe` contains lifted game code (from `tools/recomp`). This is the risk.
- `cache_seed` (s36, `package.ps1 -Seed`) holds translated game shaders: also derived data.
- The Ryujinx translator itself is NOT a risk (MIT, credited in README). Its cost is the .NET
  runtime + Ryujinx files, which we accept.

## Target release layout

Ships: launcher.exe, runtime (as a static lib or object files), lifter `tools/recomp`, the
shader sidecar `tools/shaderc` (+ .NET runtime, or self-contained publish), a bundled
compiler toolchain (clang + lld + Windows SDK libs we may redistribute; check licences),
hook/address tables, data/ (subtitles etc., our own text only), LICENSE, README.
Never ships: tms.exe, generated .cpp, cache_seed, any game file.

## Phases (do in this order; each one is useful alone)

### Phase 1: offline all-shader translation (do first, smallest)

- Find where the game keeps shader binaries (NVN program blobs inside the game's archives /
  romfs). Same idea as `tools/texextract` (offline texture scan, same hashes as runtime).
- New tool (e.g. `tools/shaderscan`): walk the user's game data, extract every shader, key it
  exactly like the runtime does, translate via the existing sidecar, write into the normal
  `<data>/cache/shaders.bin`. Runtime then does 0 translations.
- Pipelines (vertex layout, blend, render-target formats) are only known at runtime. Keep the
  s36 recipes + prewarm for that part. Option to look at: record a generic recipe set made of
  OUR state descriptions only (no game bytes) and ship it, so prewarm can build most pipelines
  on first start. Check whether a recipe contains game-derived bytes before shipping it.
- Done when: fresh `<data>/cache`, run the scan, play new areas, hitch log shows no shader
  translations and pipeline creation near the s36 seeded number (36 ms).

Unknowns: does the game keep all shaders in files, or build/patch any at runtime? Do the
uncensor patches / UHD pack change shader blobs? (Most likely not, but check: the cache key
must still match.)

### Phase 2: build the game on the user's PC

- Launcher setup page: pick game folder (NSP, or extracted folder) -> verify -> lift -> compile
  -> link -> tms.exe in the install folder -> (optional) Phase 1 shader scan.
- Version check is required: all hooks use fixed addresses for the ASIA base (title
  0100A9400C9C2000). Hash main/sdk NSOs and refuse unknown versions with a clear message
  (list the supported version like SavageWind does). Other regions/updates = their own
  address tables later, not now.
- Keys: needs the user's own prod.keys to decrypt the NSP. Ask for the file in setup (same as
  emulators). Never ship keys. Supporting an already-extracted folder avoids keys entirely.
- Must reuse the dev build path (same lifter flags, same CMake/ninja steps) so dev and setup
  never differ. One script, two callers.

### Phase 3: package

- `tools/package/package.ps1`: new mode that builds the tools-only ZIP and asserts it has no
  tms.exe, no generated code, no cache_seed (fail the build if found).
- UHD pack ZIP: textures are upscaled game textures = derived data. Same problem as the
  seed. Options: ship the upscale pipeline (needs Real-ESRGAN, ~10 h, big) or keep the pack as
  a separate, clearly marked download. Needs a user decision.

## What a NEW user sees (consequences)

- Bigger first step: pick game folder (+ keys if NSP), wait. Estimate: lift + compile maybe
  5-20 min (measure our own build time and say the real number on screen), shader scan a few
  more minutes, disk ~1-2 GB extra. Must show progress, time left, and a working Cancel.
- Toolchain download or bundle size: clang + libs is hundreds of MB. Bundled = big ZIP,
  downloaded = needs internet at setup.
- Antivirus: an app that runs a compiler and writes a fresh exe can trigger heuristics. Keep
  everything inside the install folder; no admin rights; document it.
- Wrong game version or bad dump: must fail early with a plain message, never a crash later.
- After setup: no stutter in new areas from the first minute (the goal).
- Updates: when we update the runtime/hooks, setup must re-run the build (fast if the lift
  output is cached; slow if not). The launcher's GitHub updater has to trigger that.

## What it means for the DEV (consequences)

- Every bug report now depends on the user's local build: log the toolchain version, lifter
  version, game hash, and build log path in issues.log.
- Build must be deterministic and work on clean machines (no paths into private/, no
  dependence on our Ghidra project or private/third_party at runtime). Test on a clean user
  account / VM.
- `tools/shaderc` dll stamp keys the shader cache (NOTES s26). The setup scan and the runtime
  must use the SAME sidecar build, or every cache is thrown away. Never rebuild shaderc
  casually; ship it pinned. The Ryujinx `spirv-no-elseif.patch` must be in the shipped build.
- The s30 rule still applies: nothing may shrink a user's cache; the scan only adds.
- Keep the current dev path (play.bat, tms.exe built here) unchanged. Setup is an extra page
  and an extra script, not a replacement. That way nothing that works now breaks.

## User decisions (2026-10-30)

1. Toolchain: "whatever is easiest" -> BUNDLE clang/lld/libs inside the ZIP (no download
   code, no internet needed at setup; cost = bigger ZIP). Check each redistribution licence.
2. Game input: user dumps their OWN game + OWN prod.keys. Setup accepts NSP + prod.keys
   (decrypt like nstool does now); an extracted folder may also be accepted. Never ship keys.
3. UHD pack: user does NOT want users upscaling (~10 h). Keep sharing the user's own
   upscaled pack as a SEPARATE optional download (as now: TMSRecomp-UHD-*.zip). Note: it is
   still derived from game textures, so it carries some risk, but HD texture packs are
   commonly shared this way and keeping it apart keeps the program download clean.
   Do not mix it into the program ZIP.
4. Phase 1 already started in a running session (10-30). Check NOTES.md for its state
   before doing anything here.

## Status (2026-10-31, session 38)

Phase 1 done + in-game checked (5 translations left in a replay, see NOTES s38). Phase 2 built: game.dll split,
tools/setup/setup.py + build_game.py, launcher Setup page; NSP mode untested. Phase 3: package.ps1 ships setup\ and
refuses game code; needs the Python embeddable package + licence texts (downloads, ask user).

## Rules still in force

No GitHub upload until the user's full game test. Ask before delete/push/publish/install.
Measure before change. Logs as proof.

```

```md
<h1 align="center">TMSRecomp</h1>

<p align="center"><b>Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore, running natively on Windows.</b><br>
Up to 4K and 240 fps · DLSS 4.5 / FSR 3 · VRR · one-click setup and updates · no emulator</p>

<p align="center">
  <a href="../../releases/latest"><img alt="Latest release" src="https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/godofknife/TMSRecomp?include_prereleases&label=release&color=3ee08f"></a>
  <a href="../../releases"><img alt="Downloads" src="https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/godofknife/TMSRecomp/total?color=3ee08f"></a>
  <img alt="Platform" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%20%7C%2011-blue">
  <img alt="Vulkan" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/graphics-Vulkan%201.3-red">
  <a href="LICENSE"><img alt="License" src="https://img.shields.io/badge/license-GPL--2.0--or--later-lightgrey"></a>
</p>

<p align="center">
  <img src="docs/screenshots/shibuya.jpg" width="49%" alt="Shibuya at 4K">
  <img src="docs/screenshots/carnage_form.jpg" width="49%" alt="Carnage Form">
  <img src="docs/screenshots/battle.jpg" width="49%" alt="Battle skill menu">
  <img src="docs/screenshots/session.jpg" width="49%" alt="Session lineup">
</p>
<p align="center"><sub>4K, DLSS, UHD textures, Xbox button prompts. Screenshots from the author's own copy.</sub></p>

**TMSRecomp** is an unofficial native Windows port of *Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore* (Nintendo Switch, ATLUS /
Intelligent Systems, 2020), made by static recompilation: the game's 32-bit ARM code is translated to C and compiled
into an ordinary Windows x64 program, and its graphics run on Vulkan. There is no emulator and no JIT
([how it works](#how-it-works)).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **No game files are included.** You need your own legally obtained copy of *Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore*, dumped
> from your own console: the base game **1.0.0 without update** (title ID `0100A9400C9C2000`) and your `prod.keys`, or an
> already extracted folder. How to dump them is not covered here, and requests for game files will be closed.
>
> The game is built from your files on your PC, so the result contains the game. It is for your own use: do not share
> `game.dll` or your game files folder.

> [!NOTE]
> **This project was built entirely with AI.** All of the code, tooling, reverse engineering and documentation in this
> repository was written by an AI model (Anthropic's Claude, through Claude Code), directed, tested and reviewed by the
> project's owner. It is shared as is, as a fan project. As with any code from the internet, you build and run it at
> your own discretion.

> [!WARNING]
> **v0.1.3 beta.** It is tested until the chapter 2 Idolasphere with
> saving and loading, on NVIDIA RTX. **Anything after that is unknown territory**, as are AMD / Intel GPUs and weaker
> PCs: bug reports are very welcome.

*TMSRecomp is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Nintendo, ATLUS, SEGA or Intelligent Systems. Tokyo Mirage
Sessions #FE Encore and all related names, characters and assets are trademarks and copyrights of their owners.*

## At a glance

| | Nintendo Switch | TMSRecomp on PC |
|---|---|---|
| Resolution | 720p | 720p to 4K, 8K supersampling |
| Frame rate | 30 fps | 30, 60, 120, 144, 165, 240 or uncapped |
| Anti-aliasing | FXAA | FXAA, SMAA, MSAA up to 8x, AMD FSR 3, NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA (DLSS 4.5 models) |
| Upscaling | none | FSR 1, FSR 3 and DLSS Quality to Ultra Performance |
| Display | TV / handheld | borderless or window, Mailbox, VSync, VRR (G-SYNC / FreeSync) |
| Textures and movies | original | optional 4x UHD texture pack and 4K movies |
| Extras | none | battle retry, revealed maps, battle speed, multipliers, fast travel, autosave, mods and more |
| Controls | Joy-Con / Pro Controller | keyboard, Xbox, PlayStation and Switch pads with matching button prompts |

## Features

**Performance and display**
- Native code, not emulation: the game's ARM code is translated to C and compiled for Windows x64, and its NVN graphics
  calls run on Vulkan. Built on your PC from your own dump in 5 to 15 minutes.
- Frame rate 30 (the game's own), 60, 120, 144, 165, 240 or uncapped. Game logic,
  animation and the camera run at the chosen rate; the game keeps its original speed.
- Internal resolution from 720p (the game's own) to 4K, and 8K supersampling; Auto picks one for your screen and GPU.
- Borderless fullscreen or window (F11 / Alt+Enter switches while playing).
- **Ultrawide** 21:9 and 32:9 (or Auto: your screen's shape): a wider 3D view, HUD and menus stay 16:9 in the middle,
  field HUD in the screen corners. Never stretched: other shapes get black bars.
- VSync modes: Mailbox (no tearing, low latency), classic VSync, **VRR** (G-SYNC / FreeSync: VSync plus a frame cap
  3 fps under your refresh rate) and Off.
- Even frame pacing: a dedicated present thread, pipeline prewarm and a shader cache built during setup, so new areas
  do not stutter.
- Weak-PC defaults: integrated GPUs and cards under 4 GB of VRAM get a lighter default resolution and no UHD pack.

**Image quality**
- Anti-aliasing: the game's FXAA, SMAA, **AMD FSR 3** (temporal, works on any GPU) or **NVIDIA DLSS / DLAA** (RTX GPUs,
  optional download from NVIDIA during setup), plus MSAA 2x / 4x / 8x.
- FSR 3 / DLSS upscaling modes: Native (DLAA), Quality, Balanced, Performance, Ultra Performance. Menus and text always
  stay at full resolution.
- DLSS model selection: Auto, K (transformer) or the DLSS 4.5 models M and L (DLSS 310.9).
- FSR 1 screen scaler and contrast-adaptive sharpening (Off / Low / Medium / High).
- Each post effect can be turned off: bloom, glow, depth of field, vignette, fog, outlines, character rim light.
- Optional UHD texture pack and 4K story movies / camp backgrounds (separate downloads, see [Extras](#extras)).

**Quality of life (all optional, in the launcher and the in-game menu)**
- In-game settings menu (F1 or L3 + R3) with live changes, and a **Travel** page: jump to shops you have visited, or
  open the Tokyo Map from anywhere.
- **Reveal dungeon maps**: each Idolasphere floor shows its whole layout on the minimap and map when you enter it.
- **Retry lost battles** with the battle's starting HP / EP / items.
- **Overworld costume**: the costume equipped for battle is also worn in town, dungeons and story scenes.
- **All difficulties unlocked**: Friendly and Lunatic from the start, and every difficulty (Friendly .. Lunatic) can be
  changed mid-game in System > Settings. See [Difficulty levels](#difficulty-levels) for what each one changes.
- Battle speed, autosave after battles (to slot 20, your own slots are untouched), field walk speed.
- EXP, money and mastery multipliers; Sub Cast EXP; EXP level-gap penalty on/off; level-ups refill HP / EP;
  fallen members revive with 1 HP after a battle; carry 99 of each item; guarding recovers HP / EP.
- First strike on downed field enemies, hide field enemies, weakness / resistance icons in battle, detailed skill help.
- English subtitles for the Japanese battle voices.
- Random battle music: the game's own tracks, your own `.adx` music folder, or both, with matching victory themes.
- Button prompts for Switch, PlayStation or Xbox controllers (Auto detects your pad), and a **Button layout** option:
  Switch (right face button confirms) or Xbox / PC (bottom button confirms).
- **Resist markers**: a shield over foes that resist the highlighted skill (also in the target panel) and a RESIST popup
  on resisted hits, next to the game's own weakness "!" and WEAK.
- **Keyboard and mouse**: every button can be rebound (up to 3 keys each, mouse buttons and wheel too), and the mouse
  turns the camera (sensitivity, invert). Launcher > Game > Keyboard & mouse.
- **Controller button remapping**: any Switch button on any pad button, back paddles included; button prompts follow.
  Launcher > Game > Controller buttons.
- DS4Windows works: its virtual pad is used and the real PlayStation pad is left to it.
- Menus and dialogue stay at their original pace at any frame rate, with optional smoothing above 60 fps.

**Launcher**
- One window for setup, settings, mods, extras and updates. Quick settings on the Play page, every option on its pages.
- **Setup page**: pick your NSP + `prod.keys` (or an extracted folder) and press SET UP. No emulator, no firmware, no
  internet needed.
- **Guide page**: explains each extra and installs it from its ZIP with one click.
- **Mods page**: turn mods on and off without deleting them.
- **One-click updates** from this repository's releases (see [Updating](#updating)).
- Copy system info and open the last log for bug reports.
- The window icon and the Play page picture come from your own game (the NSP's icon and your title screen).

- **Controller button remapping** (new, issue #7): Launcher > Game > Controller buttons. Pick the pad button for A, B, X,
  Y, L, R, ZL, ZR, +, -, L3 and R3 with the arrows: face buttons, bumpers, triggers, Start / Back, stick clicks or back
  paddles (Legion Go, Steam Deck, Xbox Elite). Taking a button another one has swaps the two. Button prompts show the
  button you really press. In `settings.ini`: `pad_a` .. `pad_r3`. The D-pad stays where it is.

- **Ultrawide** (new): Aspect ratio 21:9, 32:9 or Auto (launcher > Display & FPS). The 3D view gets wider; HUD and menus
  stay 16:9 in the middle; the field HUD (minimap, CALL ring, party panel) sits in the screen corners; bars and the
  battle RESULTS panels continue to the screen edges. Fixed pictures (title screen, camp background, Tokyo Map, battle
  start cut-in) stay 16:9 in the middle instead of stretching. Default 16:9 is unchanged.
- **Keyboard and mouse** (new): rebind every button and stick direction (up to 3 keys each, mouse buttons and wheel
  too) on the launcher's Game page, or `key_<button>` in `settings.ini`. The mouse turns the camera while the game has
  focus (F1 menu or Alt+Tab frees the pointer); sensitivity and invert settings.
- **Resist markers** (new, on by default): when a skill is highlighted, foes that resist it get a shield where the game
  shows "!" for a weakness, also in the target panel's circle; a resisted hit shows a RESIST popup like WEAK.
- **Button layout** (new): Xbox / PC makes the bottom face button confirm (A/B and X/Y swapped); prompts follow.
- **DS4Windows**: with DS4Windows running, the game uses its virtual pad (fixes a pad that dropped and kept a button held).
- **Linux (experimental)**, contributed by XCyrexX: a native Linux build from source. See [Linux](#linux-experimental).
- Possible fix for a blank / frozen picture with working audio (issue #3), not confirmed yet.
- After updating, the first battles and areas stutter once while the new shaders compile.

## What's new in v0.1.1

- **Overworld costume** (new, off by default): party members wear their equipped costume outside battle too: town,
  dungeons and story scenes. Launcher Game page, in-game menu (F1 / L3 + R3) or System > Settings PC 4/4.
- **Unlock all difficulties** (new, on by default): Friendly and Lunatic can be chosen from the start, and the Settings
  difficulty row goes from Friendly to Lunatic at any time (the original allows Lunatic only on a new game).
- **Setup: NSPs with a ticket now work.** NSPs whose game data is locked with a title key (the ticket `.tik` is inside the
  NSP) failed with a "title.keys" message; setup now uses the NSP's own ticket. `title.keys` is not needed.
- **Extras replace older versions**: installing a newer uncensor patch removes the old patch mod; a new UHD / MovieHD ZIP
  removes the files the old pack had.
- After updating, the launcher rebuilds `game.dll` once (a few minutes): setup changed.

## Requirements

- Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
- A GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and a current driver (NVIDIA GTX 900 series or newer, AMD RX 400 or newer, Intel Arc or
  recent integrated graphics). Only NVIDIA RTX has been tested so far.
- About 15 GB of free disk space (game files plus the built game). The UHD texture pack and 4K movies need more.
- Your own dump of the game: an NSP of the base game 1.0.0 and `prod.keys` from your own Switch, or an already extracted
  folder with `exefs\` and `romfs\` (no keys needed then).
- Nothing else: Python, the compiler and the shader translator ship inside the ZIP.

## Installing and playing

1. Download `TMSRecomp-<date>.zip` from the [Releases](../../releases) page and extract it anywhere you can write to
   (for example `D:\Games\TMSRecomp`, not `C:\Program Files`).
2. Run `launcher.exe`. The **Setup** page opens.
3. Pick your game: **NSP file…** plus your `prod.keys`, or **Extracted folder…**. Optionally tick **Download NVIDIA DLSS**
   (RTX GPUs).
4. Press **SET UP**. Setup copies the game files (about 13 GB), translates the game code, compiles it into `game.dll`
   and translates all shaders. It takes about 5 to 15 minutes and shows its progress.
5. Press **PLAY**.

The exe is not signed, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on the first start ("More info" > "Run anyway"). Some antivirus
tools look closely at a program that runs a compiler; everything stays inside the TMSRecomp folder.

Command line: `tms.exe --data <folder>` uses another game files folder; `--set key=value` overrides any setting for one
run (repeatable), for example `tms.exe --set window=window --set res=1080p --set fps=60`.

## Updating

The launcher checks this repository for a new release each time it starts.

1. When a new version is out, the launcher shows **Version x.y.z is ready**. **What's new** opens the release notes.
2. Press **Update**, then **Yes**. The launcher downloads the release, replaces its program files and restarts.
3. If the new version changes the game code, the Setup page rebuilds `game.dll` from your existing game files by
   itself (a few minutes; your NSP is not needed again).

Your `settings.ini`, saves, mods, UHD textures, movies and music are never touched by an update. **Check again** below
the version box checks manually. You can also update by hand: extract the new ZIP over your folder and replace the files.

## Extras

The launcher's **Guide** page explains each extra and installs it: press **Install ZIP…** (or **Install patch…**) and
pick the file you downloaded.

| Extra | What it does | Where to get it |
|---|---|---|
| English patch & uncensor | English voices and uncensored outfits / art (community patches) | the patch's own page; the Guide links it |
| UHD textures | AI-upscaled textures, 4x (`TMSRecomp-UHD` ZIP) | link in the release notes |
| 4K movies | 4K story movies and camp menu backgrounds (`TMSRecomp-MovieHD` ZIP) | link in the release notes |
| Your own battle music | random battle tracks from your own `.adx` files (for example a Persona 5 Royal music mod) | your own files |

Installing a newer version of an extra replaces the older one: an updated patch removes the old patch mod (mods with
other content stay), and a new UHD / MovieHD ZIP removes files the old pack had and the new one does not. Every extra
is optional; the game works the same without them. The UHD textures can be turned off without uninstalling
(launcher Graphics page or the in-game menu, after a restart).

| Move | W A S D | left stick |
| Camera | mouse (or keys you bind) | right stick |

| X / Y | I / U | X / Y |
| L / R, ZL / ZR | Q / E, 1 / 3 | L / R, ZL / ZR |

In the Y menu, (-) offers Return to Title or Quit Game. Every keyboard / mouse key can be changed on the launcher's Game
page (Keyboard & mouse), or in `settings.ini` with `key_<button> = Key, Key, Key` (SDL key names such as `K`, `Return`,
`Left Shift`, `Keypad 4`, plus `Mouse1` .. `Mouse5`, `WheelUp`, `WheelDown`, `none`).

## Settings

Change settings in the launcher (Save, then PLAY) or in the in-game menu (F1 / L3 + R3; most apply at once). They are
stored in `settings.ini` next to `tms.exe` as `key = value`; any key can also be set with the environment variable
`NX_<KEY>` or `--set key=value`.

| Key | Values | |
|---|---|---|
| `fps` | 30, 60 (default), any number above 60, 0 = uncapped | frame rate |
| `res` | auto (default), 720p, 1080p, 1440p, 4k, 8k | internal resolution |
| `window` | borderless (default), window | |
| `present_mode` | mailbox (default), fifo, vrr, immediate | VSync |
| `fx_fxaa` | 0 off, 1 FXAA (default), 2 SMAA, 3 FSR 3, 4 DLSS | anti-aliasing |
| `fsr3_quality` | 0 native (default), 1 Quality, 2 Balanced, 3 Performance, 4 Ultra Performance | FSR 3 / DLSS upscaling |
| `dlss_preset` | 0 auto (default), 11 K, 13 M, 12 L | DLSS model |
| `msaa` | 0 (default), 2, 4, 8 | not used with FSR 3 / DLSS |
| `upscaler` | fsr1 (default), bilinear | screen scaler below your screen size |
| `sharpen` | 0 (default) .. 100 | |
| `post_native` | 1 (default), 0 | depth of field / bloom at the game's size (no halos) |
| `fx_bloom`, `fx_glow`, `fx_dof`, `fx_vignette`, `fx_fog`, `fx_outline`, `fx_char_rim` | 0 turns the effect off | |
| `tex_pack` | auto (default), 1, 0 | UHD texture pack |
| `pad_icons` | auto (default), switch, playstation, xbox | button prompts |
| `button_layout` | switch (default), xbox | which face button confirms |
| `aspect` | 16:9 (default), auto, 21:9, 32:9 | ultrawide |
| `resist_marker` | 1 (default), 0 | resist shield / RESIST popup in battle |
| `key_a` .. `key_rs_right` | key names, comma separated | keyboard / mouse bindings (see [Controls](#controls)) |
| `mouse_camera`, `mouse_sensitivity`, `mouse_invert_y` | 1, 1.0 (0.2 .. 3.0), 0 | mouse turns the camera |
| `pad_a` .. `pad_r3` | default, south, east, west, north, lb, rb, lt, rt, start, back, ls, rs, paddle1 .. paddle4, none | controller button remapping (launcher > Game > Controller buttons); taking another button's swaps the two |
| `walk_speed` | 1.0 (default) .. 3.0 | field walk speed |
| `map_reveal` | 0 (default), 1 | reveal dungeon maps |
| `field_costume` | 0 (default), 1 | overworld costume |
| `all_difficulties` | 1 (default), 0 | Friendly / Lunatic unlocked, full difficulty range in Settings |
| `battle_retry` | 1 (default), 0 | retry lost battles |
| `autosave` | 1 (default), 0 | save to slot 20 after battles |
| `exp_rate`, `money_rate`, `mastery_rate` | 1 (default) and up | multipliers |
| `sub_exp`, `exp_gap`, `levelup_refill`, `ko_revive`, `item_max99`, `guard_regen`, `first_strike` | 1 / 0 | gameplay extras |
| `random_battle_bgm` | 0 off, 1 game tracks, 2 custom, 3 mixed | with `custom_bgm_dir`, `custom_bgm_volume` (0 .. 10) |
| `voice_subs` | 1 (default), 0 | English battle voice subtitles |
| `ui_speed`, `ui_smooth` | 60 / 1 (defaults) | menu pace and smoothing above 60 fps |
| `mute` | 1 | sound off |
| `mods_disabled` | folder names, comma separated | mods to leave off |
| `data` | a folder | the game files folder |

The full list with explanations is at the top of `settings.ini` and in the ZIP's `README.txt`.

## Saves

The game's own save files live unchanged in `save\` inside your game files folder (`system.bin`, `save_*.bin`). Back
that folder up now and then. Autosave (on by default) writes slot 20 after battles and never touches your own slots.

**Emulator saves** (Ryujinx or a Yuzu-based emulator) use the same files and should load (not tested yet, please
report how it goes):

1. Back up the `save\` folder in your game files folder.
2. In the emulator, right-click the game > **Open User Save Directory** (Ryujinx) or **Open Save Data Location**.
3. Copy `system.bin` and every `save_*.bin` from there into `save\`.
4. PLAY and pick LOAD.

A save written by an updated game (not 1.0.0) is untested.

## Mods

A mod is a folder `<game files>\mods\<ModName>\` (LayeredFS style); the launcher's **Mods** page turns each one on or off.

- **Game files**: put them in `mods\<ModName>\romfs\` at the same path as in `<game files>\romfs\` (setup extracts the
  game there, so you can copy a file out, change it and put it in your mod). Files you do not ship come from the game.
  Mods shipped as xdelta patches against the game's `.cpk` files:
  `python tools/vcdiff.py <original.cpk> <patch.xdelta> <out.cpk>`.
- **Textures**: set `tex_dump = 1` and play: every texture shown is saved once to
  `<game files>\textures\dump\<w>x<h>_<format>_<hash>.dds`. Edit one, keep the `_<hash>` at the end of the name, and
  put it in `mods\<ModName>\textures\` (subfolders are fine). Any size works; DDS in BC1-BC7 or RGBA8 with mipmaps
  (`texconv -m 0`). Mod textures win over the UHD pack.
- **Several mods**: for the same file or texture, the mod whose folder name sorts first wins.
- `nx.log` lists each mod at start (`fs: mod <name> on`, `textures: mod <name>: N`). Restart the game after a change.

### Difficulty levels

What each difficulty changes, read from the game's code (battle setup and damage formula):

| Difficulty | Damage you deal | Damage you take | Money | Escape base chance |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Friendly | ×1.5 | ×0.5 | ×1.25 | 50% |
| Easy | ×1.25 | ×0.8 | ×1.25 | 50% |
| Normal | ×1.0 | ×1.0 | ×1.0 | 30% |
| Hard | ×0.8 | ×1.25 | ×1.0 | 1% |
| Lunatic | ×0.5 | ×1.5 | ×1.0 | 1% |

Hard and Lunatic also change ailment hit rates; on Friendly and Easy, members below the enemy's level get +20% EXP per
level instead of +10%. Enemy HP and stats are the same on every difficulty.

## Troubleshooting and FAQ

- **Setup fails or stops.** The Setup page shows the step and the error; **Open last log** shows the details. Check
  that the NSP is the base game 1.0.0 (not an update or DLC) and that `prod.keys` comes from your own console. A
  message about `title.keys` alone is only a warning; since v0.1.1 an NSP's own ticket is used. If setup still says the
  NSP needs a title key, put `title.keys` (with this game's key) next to `prod.keys`. With an
  extracted folder, it must contain `exefs\main` and `romfs\`.
- **"The game is not set up yet, or needs a rebuild after an update."** Open the Setup page; it rebuilds `game.dll`
  from your existing files.
- **DLSS is not offered or falls back to FSR 3.** DLSS needs an RTX GPU, a current NVIDIA driver and `nvngx_dlss.dll`
  next to `tms.exe` (Setup page > Download NVIDIA DLSS).
- **Stutter the first time something appears.** Pipelines are compiled once and cached in `<game files>\cache`;
  the second time is smooth. Do not delete that folder.
- **Low fps.** Lower the resolution, use FSR 3 / DLSS upscaling (Quality or Balanced), turn MSAA off. 60 fps is the
  most tested frame rate.
- **Screen tearing with VRR.** Turn on G-SYNC / FreeSync in your GPU driver and use VSync = VRR in the launcher.
- **The game does not start / closes at once.** Update your GPU driver, then send the bug report described below.
- **Can I use an updated game (1.0.1+) or DLC?** Not yet: the hooks use fixed addresses of the 1.0.0 build.
- **Linux / Steam Deck?** An experimental native Linux build can be built from source: see [Linux (experimental)](#linux-experimental). Proton is untested.
- **Where are my files?** Everything (game files, saves, cache, logs, screenshots, mods) is in the game files folder
  chosen during setup; settings are in `settings.ini` next to `tms.exe`.

## Known issues

- Tested from the start through chapter 2 only; later chapters may have problems nobody has seen yet.
- Tested on NVIDIA RTX only (Linux: one NVIDIA GTX 1650). AMD and Intel GPUs, integrated GPUs and Steam Deck are untested.
- Only the base game 1.0.0 without update is supported.
- Walking NPCs turn in small 30 Hz steps at high frame rates.
- Custom battle music: encrypted `.adx` files need their key in `settings.ini` (`custom_bgm_key`); none is included.
- Ray tracing is not planned: the game's lighting is baked into its art.

## Reporting a bug

A good report lets us find and fix the problem quickly. Please open an issue with the **bug report** form and include:

1. **Your PC (spec rig):** launcher > **Guide** > Controls & help > **Copy system info**, then paste it. It lists your
   CPU, GPU, driver, RAM, Windows version and settings.
2. **What happened:** what you did, what you saw and what you expected instead. Does it happen every time?
3. **Where:** chapter, place, and menu or battle.
4. **Screenshot or video:** F12 saves a screenshot to `<game files>\shots`. A short video helps most with flicker,
   stutter or animation problems.
5. **Save data:** zip the `save\` folder in your game files folder and attach it, and say which slot to load. We can
   then go straight to the spot.
6. **Log:** attach `nx.log` from your game files folder (and `issues.log` if there is one). Copy it **before** you start
   the game again: each start writes a new log.

Never post game files, keys or links to them.

## How it works

- `tools/nso.py`, `tools/cpk.py`: readers for the game's executables (NSO) and CRI archives (CPK).
- `tools/recomp/`: our A32 (ARMv7 / ARMv8-AArch32) to C recompiler. It links `main` + `sdk` like the Switch's loader,
  finds functions and emits one C function per guest function; `test_a32.py` checks the translation against Unicorn.
- `runtime/`: guest memory, a high-level Horizon kernel (threads, synchronisation, memory SVCs), the `nn::` services the
  game uses (fs, hid, vi, audio, ...), NVN implemented on Vulkan, and the PC extras (in-game menu, upscalers, mods).
- `tools/shaderc/`: a sidecar that turns the game's Maxwell shaders into SPIR-V with the Ryujinx shader translator.
- `tools/setup/`: the player's first-run setup (extract, recompile, build `game.dll`, translate shaders).
- `runtime/launcher/`: the launcher (Win32 + Direct2D).
- `NOTES.md`: the full technical log of the project.

## Linux (experimental)

A native Linux x86-64 build of the same runtime, launcher and setup (no Wine or Proton). As on Windows, the game is
built on your PC from your own dump; nothing of the game is in the repository or a build.

**Tested so far** (Ubuntu 26.04, NVIDIA GTX 1650, driver 620): setup from an extracted folder, launcher, title screen,
intro movie, story scenes, field, camp menu, saving and loading, the F1 menu, at a steady 60 fps. Battles, AMD and Intel
GPUs and the Steam Deck are not tested yet.

**Differences from Windows**
- No AMD FSR 3 and no NVIDIA DLSS: AMD ships the FidelityFX API only as Windows DLLs, and the NGX (DLSS) path is not
  wired up. Choosing them falls back to SMAA, as on a Windows PC without them. FXAA, SMAA, MSAA, FSR 1 and sharpening work.
- The launcher's Update button opens the release page (releases are Windows downloads).
- `settings.ini` sits next to `tms` when that folder is writable, else in `~/.config/TMSRecomp/settings.ini` (an
  AppImage or system install); `NX_INI` overrides it. The recompiled code is `game.so` next to `tms`, or where
  `NX_GAME_SO` points.
- The Windows-only debugging aids (`NX_PROFILE`, `NX_CONTROL watch`, `NX_STALL_STATS`, `NX_MEM_REGIONS`) say they are
  not available; use `perf` instead.
- File names in the game files folder are matched case-insensitively, as on Windows.

**Packages** (Ubuntu / Debian names; other distributions have the same libraries): `clang lld llvm cmake ninja-build
pkg-config libsdl3-dev libvulkan-dev libvpx-dev libcairo2-dev libpango1.0-dev python3-venv dotnet-sdk-10.0`, and
nstool 1.9.2 built from source (`make deps && make`). Capstone for the translator:
`python3 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install capstone`.

**Build** (the same third-party Ryujinx checkout and patch as on Windows, in `private/third_party/ryubing`):

1. `clang -O2 -shared -fPIC -o tools/texextract/fasttex.so tools/texextract/fasttex.c`
2. `dotnet build tools/shaderc/NxShader.csproj -c Release -o private/tms/shaderc`
3. Set up the game data folder with your own dump, compile `game.so` and translate all shaders:
   `venv/bin/python tools/setup/setup.py --nsp <game.nsp> --keys <prod.keys> --data private/tms --nstool <nstool> --install private/tms/build`
   (or `--folder <extracted folder>` instead of `--nsp` / `--keys` / `--data`). This writes `private/tms/gen`.
4. `cmake -S . -B private/tms/build -G Ninja -DCMAKE_C_COMPILER=clang -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=clang++ -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo`
   and `ninja -C private/tms/build tms launcher` (`ninja -C private/tms/build` also rebuilds `game.so`).
5. Run `private/tms/build/launcher`, or `private/tms/build/tms --data private/tms`.

The Linux code paths are marked `#ifdef _WIN32 ... #else` in place; `runtime/src/plat.h` has the small POSIX stand-ins,
`runtime/src/draw_linux.h` the cairo / pango drawing (menu, subtitles, button icons) and `runtime/launcher/linux_shim.h`
the launcher's window layer (SDL3). Guest memory write tracking (texture re-uploads) uses page protection in place of
Windows' write watch (`memory.cpp`).

## Building from source

Requirements: Visual Studio 2022 (CMake + Ninja), LLVM/clang, .NET 10 SDK, Python 3.12, a Vulkan 1.3 GPU.
Third-party pieces go in `private/third_party/`: SDL3 3.4.16 (VC dev package), Vulkan-Headers 1.4.328, nstool 1.9.2,
the Ryujinx (Ryubing) source for the shader sidecar, libvpx 1.16.0 (BSD-3-Clause, VP9 movies) and the AMD FidelityFX /
FSR SDK 2.4.0 files used by FSR 3 (`FidelityFX-SDK-2.4.0/Kits/FidelityFX`: api/include, upscalers/include,
signedbin/amd_fidelityfx_*_vk.dll, docs/license.md; only MIT-listed files). Apply `tools/shaderc/patches/*.patch` to the
Ryujinx checkout (`patch -p1` from its root): its SPIR-V backend drops `else if` branches otherwise.

1. Extract your NSP with nstool and your own `prod.keys` into `private/tms/` (`exefs/`, `romfs/`).
2. `python tools/recomp/link.py private/tms/exefs private/tms/link`
3. `python tools/recomp/lift.py private/tms/link private/tms/gen`
4. `dotnet build tools/shaderc/NxShader.csproj -c Release -o private/tms/shaderc`
   (release ZIP only: `dotnet publish tools/shaderc/NxShader.csproj -c Release -r win-x64 --self-contained true -o
   private/tms/shaderc_sc -p:DebugType=none -p:SatelliteResourceLanguages=en`, then `cp -p private/tms/shaderc/*.dll
   private/tms/shaderc_sc/` so the shader cache stamp stays the same).
5. libvpx (Git Bash, from `private/third_party`, LLVM on `PATH`; a portable C build, no assembler needed):
   `git clone --depth 1 --branch v1.16.0 https://github.com/webmproject/libvpx.git`, then in a new `vpx-gen` folder
   `CC=clang ../libvpx/configure --target=generic-gnu --disable-vp8 --disable-vp9-encoder --disable-examples --disable-tools --disable-docs --disable-unit-tests --disable-webm-io --disable-libyuv`,
   generate the headers `make` would (`perl ../libvpx/build/make/rtcd.pl --arch=generic --sym=<name> --config=libs-generic-gnu.mk <defs> > <name>.h`
   for `vp9_rtcd` (`vp9/common/vp9_rtcd_defs.pl`), `vpx_dsp_rtcd` (`vpx_dsp/vpx_dsp_rtcd_defs.pl`), `vpx_scale_rtcd`
   (`vpx_scale/vpx_scale_rtcd.pl`), and `sh ../libvpx/build/make/version.sh ../libvpx vpx_version.h`), then list the
   sources: `python tools/vpx_sources.py private/third_party/libvpx private/third_party/vpx-gen`.
6. `build.cmd` builds `tms.exe` (the runtime) and `game.dll` (the lifted code, through `tools/setup/build_game.py`, the
   same script the player's setup uses). Run `private/tms/build/tms.exe`; it finds the data folder `private/tms` from its
   own location.
7. Release ZIP: `powershell -File tools/package/package.ps1` writes `TMSRecomp-<date>.zip` to the Desktop.
8. Optional: `tools/make_icon.ps1 <image>` makes `private/tms/icon.ico` for your own build; `tools/make_shortcut.ps1`
   puts a launcher shortcut on your Desktop.

UHD textures from your own copy: play with `tex_dump = 1`, then `python tools/uhd_pack.py private/tms` (needs
Real-ESRGAN-ncnn-vulkan, texconv and ImageMagick; see the script). Without playing: `python
tools/texextract/texextract.py private/tms` dumps every texture, then `python tools/uhd_pack.py private/tms --dump
private/tms/textures/dump_all`. 4K camp backgrounds: `python tools/camphd/camphd.py <data> <esrgan dir>`.

Everything derived from the game (decrypted files, the linked image, generated C code, shaders, builds) stays in
`private/`, which is never committed.
```

`play.bat`:

```bat
@echo off
rem Play TMSRecomp. The game writes its full log to private\tms\live.log; this window shows only problems
rem (private\tms\issues.log) as they happen, with the time. The previous run's logs move to private\tms\logs\.
rem Close this window after the game.
cd /d "%~dp0private\tms"
if not exist build\tms.exe (echo build\tms.exe not found: run build.cmd first & pause & exit /b 1)
set NX_LOG=live.log
rem window, internal resolution and frame rate: private\tms\build\settings.ini (written on the first run)
rem every run records the pad input the game reads (input.rec, replay with NX_REPLAY=...); old ones go to logs\
set NX_RECORD=input.rec
rem play.bat 60: game logic at 60 fps; play.bat 144 (any N > 60): capped at N; play.bat 0: uncapped (default: settings.ini)
if not "%1"=="" set NX_FPS=%1
start "" /b cmd /c "build\tms.exe --data . 2>nul >nul"
rem wait until the game has created the new issues.log, then follow it
:wait
timeout /t 1 /nobreak >nul
if not exist issues.log goto wait
title TMSRecomp - live issues (problems only; full log: private\tms\live.log)
powershell -NoProfile -Command "Get-Content -Path issues.log -Wait -Tail 50"

```

`runtime/include/guest.h`:

```h
/* Guest CPU state and helpers used by the recompiled code (C11 and C++).
 * Guest memory is one 4 GiB window at a fixed host address, so a guest address is just an offset. */
#pragma once
#ifdef NX_GAME_DLL
/* game.dll (the recompiled code) is built on the player's PC with only clang + lld-link (tools/setup/build_game.py):
 * no C library headers. Runtime entry points are imported from tms.exe, the few C library functions the code calls
 * from the CRT DLLs tms.exe already uses (import libs made from tools/setup/nx_*.def). Declarations match the MSVC headers. */
typedef __INT8_TYPE__ int8_t;
typedef __INT16_TYPE__ int16_t;
typedef __INT32_TYPE__ int32_t;
typedef __INT64_TYPE__ int64_t;
typedef __UINT8_TYPE__ uint8_t;
typedef __UINT16_TYPE__ uint16_t;
typedef __UINT32_TYPE__ uint32_t;
typedef __UINT64_TYPE__ uint64_t;
typedef __SIZE_TYPE__ size_t;
#define INT32_MIN (-__INT32_MAX__ - 1)
#define INT32_MAX __INT32_MAX__
#define UINT32_MAX __UINT32_MAX__
#define INT64_MIN (-__INT64_MAX__ - 1)
#define INT64_MAX __INT64_MAX__
#define UINT64_MAX __UINT64_MAX__
#define INFINITY __builtin_inff()
#define NAN __builtin_nanf("")
#define memcpy __builtin_memcpy
double sqrt(double);
float sqrtf(float);
double floor(double);
float floorf(float);
double ceil(double);
float ceilf(float);
double round(double);
float roundf(float);
double trunc(double);
float truncf(float);
double nearbyint(double);
float nearbyintf(float);
double fabs(double);
float fabsf(float);
double fmin(double, double);
float fminf(float, float);
double fmax(double, double);
float fmaxf(float, float);
#ifdef _WIN32
typedef struct __declspec(align(16)) { unsigned long long Part[2]; } _SETJMP_FLOAT128;
typedef _SETJMP_FLOAT128 jmp_buf[16];
int __cdecl _setjmp(jmp_buf);
#define setjmp _setjmp
#define NX_API __declspec(dllimport)
#else
/* Linux (game.so): glibc's x86-64 jmp_buf (struct __jmp_buf_tag[1], 200 bytes); _setjmp does not save the signal mask.
 * The C library functions resolve against the libc / libm that tms already loaded. */
typedef long long jmp_buf[25];
int _setjmp(jmp_buf);
#define setjmp _setjmp
#define NX_API __attribute__((visibility("default")))
#endif
#else
#include <math.h>
#include <setjmp.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#ifdef _WIN32
#define NX_API __declspec(dllexport) /* tms.exe exports what game.dll calls */
#else
#define NX_API __attribute__((visibility("default"))) /* tms (linked with -rdynamic) exports what game.so calls */
#endif
#endif

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

#define GUEST_BASE 0x10000000000ull /* 1 TiB: reserved at startup with VirtualAlloc at this exact address */

typedef struct Cpu {
    uint32_t r[16];
    uint8_t n, z, cf, v;           /* APSR flags as 0/1 */
    uint8_t q, fn, fz, fc, fv;     /* sticky Q, FPSCR NZCV */
    uint8_t excl_valid, excl_size, pad0;
    uint32_t ge;                   /* GE[3:0] */
    uint32_t fpscr;                /* control bits only; NZCV live in fn..fv */
    uint32_t sh_carry;             /* carry out of the last register-shifted operand */
    uint32_t tpidruro, tpidrurw;   /* TLS registers (cp15 c13) */
    uint32_t excl_addr;
    uint64_t excl_val;
    union {
        float f[64];
        uint32_t w[64];
        double d[32];
        uint64_t x[32];
    } vr;                          /* S0-S31 alias D0-D15; D16-D31; Qn = D2n:D2n+1 */
    void* host;                    /* runtime thread object */
    uint32_t hook_bypass;          /* hook slot + 1 whose next entry runs the guest code (call_unhooked), 0 = none */
} Cpu;

typedef void (*GuestFn)(Cpu*);
typedef struct { uint32_t addr; GuestFn fn; } GuestFunc;
typedef struct { const char* name; uint32_t addr; } GuestHookName;
typedef struct {
    const char* name;
    uint32_t base, size, text_lo, text_hi, ro_lo, ro_hi, data_lo, data_hi, init;
} GuestModule;

#ifdef NX_GAME_DLL
/* defined in table.c; tms.exe reaches them (and the other tables) through game.dll's exports (dispatch.cpp game_load) */
#ifdef _WIN32
extern GuestFn g_hooks[];
extern GuestFn g_probes[];  /* observers of names-file functions: run at entry, then the function itself */
#else
/* game.so is compiled with -fvisibility=hidden (direct calls between the generated files, no PLT); these declarations
 * give table.c's definitions default visibility, so they are the library's only exports (dispatch.cpp game_load) */
#define NX_TABLE extern __attribute__((visibility("default")))
NX_TABLE GuestFn g_hooks[];
NX_TABLE GuestFn g_probes[];  /* observers of names-file functions: run at entry, then the function itself */
NX_TABLE const GuestFunc g_guest_funcs[];
NX_TABLE const uint32_t g_guest_func_count;
NX_TABLE const GuestHookName g_hook_names[];
NX_TABLE const uint32_t g_hook_count;
NX_TABLE const GuestHookName g_hook_aliases[];
NX_TABLE const uint32_t g_hook_alias_count;
NX_TABLE const GuestHookName g_thunks[];
NX_TABLE const uint32_t g_thunk_count;
NX_TABLE const GuestModule g_modules[];
NX_TABLE const uint32_t g_module_count;
NX_TABLE const uint32_t g_image_size;
#undef NX_TABLE
#endif
#endif

/* runtime entry points (runtime/src) */
NX_API void dispatch(Cpu* c, uint32_t target);
NX_API void guest_trap(Cpu* c, uint32_t addr, const char* why);
NX_API void guest_unimpl(Cpu* c, uint32_t addr, uint32_t word);
NX_API void guest_bad_branch(Cpu* c, uint32_t from, uint32_t to);
NX_API void guest_noreturn(Cpu* c, uint32_t addr);
NX_API void guest_svc(Cpu* c, uint32_t imm, uint32_t addr);
NX_API void guest_yield(Cpu* c);
NX_API uint32_t cp15_read(Cpu* c, int opc1, int crn, int crm, int opc2);
NX_API void cp15_write(Cpu* c, int opc1, int crn, int crm, int opc2, uint32_t v);

NX_API uint64_t guest_counter(void);  /* CNTPCT, 19.2 MHz */

/* setjmp/longjmp: host jump buffer + saved guest callee-saved state, keyed by the guest jmp_buf address.
 * The host side is the C runtime's setjmp: it restores all non-volatile registers (locals such as `c` survive),
 * and longjmp unwinds the recompiled frames between (they carry unwind info). */
typedef struct GuestJmp {
    jmp_buf host;
    uint32_t r[16];
    uint64_t d[8];          /* d8-d15 */
    uint32_t val;
} GuestJmp;
NX_API GuestJmp* guest_setjmp_slot(Cpu* c, uint32_t guest_buf);
NX_API void guest_setjmp_save(Cpu* c, GuestJmp* j);
NX_API void guest_setjmp_resume(Cpu* c, GuestJmp* j);

#define HOOK(i) do { if (g_hooks[i]) { if (c->hook_bypass == (i) + 1u) c->hook_bypass = 0; else { g_hooks[i](c); return; } } } while (0)
NX_API extern uint32_t* g_cover;  /* NX_COVER: call counts per hook slot */
#define PROBE(i) do { if (g_cover) g_cover[i]++; if (g_probes[i]) g_probes[i](c); } while (0)
#define JUMP(t) do { if ((t) == ret0) return; dispatch(c, (t)); return; } while (0)

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- memory */
#define GPTR(a) ((uint8_t*)(GUEST_BASE + (uint64_t)(uint32_t)(a)))
static inline uint32_t ld32(uint32_t a) { uint32_t v; memcpy(&v, GPTR(a), 4); return v; }
static inline uint32_t ld16(uint32_t a) { uint16_t v; memcpy(&v, GPTR(a), 2); return v; }
static inline uint32_t ld8(uint32_t a) { return *GPTR(a); }
static inline uint32_t lds16(uint32_t a) { int16_t v; memcpy(&v, GPTR(a), 2); return (uint32_t)(int32_t)v; }
static inline uint32_t lds8(uint32_t a) { return (uint32_t)(int32_t)(int8_t)*GPTR(a); }
static inline uint64_t ld64(uint32_t a) { uint64_t v; memcpy(&v, GPTR(a), 8); return v; }
static inline void st32(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { memcpy(GPTR(a), &v, 4); }
static inline void st16(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { uint16_t h = (uint16_t)v; memcpy(GPTR(a), &h, 2); }
static inline void st8(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { *GPTR(a) = (uint8_t)v; }
static inline void st64(uint32_t a, uint64_t v) { memcpy(GPTR(a), &v, 8); }

/* exclusive monitor: a store-exclusive succeeds if memory still holds what the load-exclusive saw (CAS) */
#define EXCL_LOAD(N, T)                                                                                     \
    static inline uint32_t excl_load##N(Cpu* c, uint32_t a) {                                             \
        T v = __atomic_load_n((T*)GPTR(a), __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);                                             \
        c->excl_addr = a; c->excl_val = v; c->excl_valid = 1; c->excl_size = N;                           \
        return (uint32_t)v;                                                                               \
    }                                                                                                     \
    static inline uint32_t excl_store##N(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, uint32_t v) {                                \
        if (!c->excl_valid || c->excl_addr != a || c->excl_size != N) { c->excl_valid = 0; return 1; }    \
        c->excl_valid = 0;                                                                                \
        T expect = (T)c->excl_val;                                                                        \
        return __atomic_compare_exchange_n((T*)GPTR(a), &expect, (T)v, 0, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST,               \
                                           __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST) ? 0 : 1;                                     \
    }
EXCL_LOAD(8, uint8_t)
EXCL_LOAD(16, uint16_t)
EXCL_LOAD(32, uint32_t)
static inline uint64_t excl_load64(Cpu* c, uint32_t a) {
    uint64_t v = __atomic_load_n((uint64_t*)GPTR(a), __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST);
    c->excl_addr = a; c->excl_val = v; c->excl_valid = 1; c->excl_size = 64;
    return v;
}
static inline uint32_t excl_store64(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, uint64_t v) {
    if (!c->excl_valid || c->excl_addr != a || c->excl_size != 64) { c->excl_valid = 0; return 1; }
    c->excl_valid = 0;
    uint64_t expect = c->excl_val;
    return __atomic_compare_exchange_n((uint64_t*)GPTR(a), &expect, v, 0, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST) ? 0 : 1;
}
/* LDA/STL (plain acquire / release, ARMv8) */
static inline uint32_t acq_load8(uint32_t a) { return __atomic_load_n(GPTR(a), __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline uint32_t acq_load16(uint32_t a) { return __atomic_load_n((uint16_t*)GPTR(a), __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline uint32_t acq_load32(uint32_t a) { return __atomic_load_n((uint32_t*)GPTR(a), __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline void rel_store8(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { __atomic_store_n(GPTR(a), (uint8_t)v, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline void rel_store16(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { __atomic_store_n((uint16_t*)GPTR(a), (uint16_t)v, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline void rel_store32(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { __atomic_store_n((uint32_t*)GPTR(a), v, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline uint32_t atomic_swap32(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { return __atomic_exchange_n((uint32_t*)GPTR(a), v, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }
static inline uint32_t atomic_swap8(uint32_t a, uint32_t v) { return __atomic_exchange_n(GPTR(a), (uint8_t)v, __ATOMIC_SEQ_CST); }

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- integer */
static inline uint32_t ror32(uint32_t v, unsigned s) { s &= 31; return s ? (v >> s) | (v << (32 - s)) : v; }
static inline void nz(Cpu* c, uint32_t r) { c->n = r >> 31; c->z = r == 0; }
static inline uint32_t add_flags(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b, uint32_t cin) {
    uint64_t s = (uint64_t)a + b + cin;
    uint32_t r = (uint32_t)s;
    c->cf = (uint8_t)(s >> 32);
    c->v = ((a ^ r) & (b ^ r)) >> 31;
    c->n = r >> 31;
    c->z = r == 0;
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t sh_lsl(uint32_t v, uint32_t s) { s &= 0xff; return s < 32 ? v << s : 0; }
static inline uint32_t sh_lsr(uint32_t v, uint32_t s) { s &= 0xff; return s < 32 ? v >> s : 0; }
static inline uint32_t sh_asr(uint32_t v, uint32_t s) { s &= 0xff; return (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> (s < 32 ? s : 31)); }
static inline uint32_t sh_ror(uint32_t v, uint32_t s) { return ror32(v, s & 31); }
static inline uint32_t sh_lsl_c(Cpu* c, uint32_t v, uint32_t s) {
    s &= 0xff;
    if (s == 0) { c->sh_carry = c->cf; return v; }
    c->sh_carry = s <= 32 ? (v >> (32 - s)) & 1 : 0;
    return s < 32 ? v << s : 0;
}
static inline uint32_t sh_lsr_c(Cpu* c, uint32_t v, uint32_t s) {
    s &= 0xff;
    if (s == 0) { c->sh_carry = c->cf; return v; }
    c->sh_carry = s <= 32 ? (v >> (s - 1)) & 1 : 0;
    return s < 32 ? v >> s : 0;
}
static inline uint32_t sh_asr_c(Cpu* c, uint32_t v, uint32_t s) {
    s &= 0xff;
    if (s == 0) { c->sh_carry = c->cf; return v; }
    if (s >= 32) { c->sh_carry = v >> 31; return (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> 31); }
    c->sh_carry = (v >> (s - 1)) & 1;
    return (uint32_t)((int32_t)v >> s);
}
static inline uint32_t sh_ror_c(Cpu* c, uint32_t v, uint32_t s) {
    s &= 0xff;
    if (s == 0) { c->sh_carry = c->cf; return v; }
    uint32_t r = ror32(v, s & 31);
    c->sh_carry = r >> 31;
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t clz32(uint32_t v) { return v ? (uint32_t)__builtin_clz(v) : 32; }
static inline uint32_t rbit32(uint32_t v) {
    v = ((v >> 1) & 0x55555555u) | ((v & 0x55555555u) << 1);
    v = ((v >> 2) & 0x33333333u) | ((v & 0x33333333u) << 2);
    v = ((v >> 4) & 0x0f0f0f0fu) | ((v & 0x0f0f0f0fu) << 4);
    return __builtin_bswap32(v);
}
static inline uint32_t sdiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    if (b == 0) return 0;
    if (a == 0x80000000u && b == 0xffffffffu) return a;
    return (uint32_t)((int32_t)a / (int32_t)b);
}
static inline uint32_t udiv32(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return b ? a / b : 0; }
static inline uint32_t usad8(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t s = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i += 8) {
        int x = (a >> i) & 0xff, y = (b >> i) & 0xff;
        s += (uint32_t)(x > y ? x - y : y - x);
    }
    return s;
}
static inline uint32_t sxtb16(uint32_t v) {
    return ((uint32_t)(int32_t)(int8_t)v & 0xffffu) | ((uint32_t)(int32_t)(int8_t)(v >> 16) << 16);
}
static inline uint32_t add16(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return ((a + b) & 0xffffu) | (((a >> 16) + (b >> 16)) << 16); }
static inline uint32_t sel_ge(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {
    uint32_t r = 0;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++) r |= ((c->ge >> i) & 1 ? a : b) & (0xffu << (8 * i));
    return r;
}
static inline uint32_t ssat(Cpu* c, int32_t v, int bits) {
    int32_t hi = (int32_t)((1u << (bits - 1)) - 1), lo = -hi - 1;
    if (v > hi) { c->q = 1; return (uint32_t)hi; }
    if (v < lo) { c->q = 1; return (uint32_t)lo; }
    return (uint32_t)v;
}
static inline uint32_t usat(Cpu* c, int32_t v, int bits) {
    int64_t hi = ((int64_t)1 << bits) - 1;
    if (v < 0) { c->q = 1; return 0; }
    if (v > hi) { c->q = 1; return (uint32_t)hi; }
    return (uint32_t)v;
}
static inline uint32_t sat32(Cpu* c, int64_t v) {
    if (v > 0x7fffffff) { c->q = 1; return 0x7fffffffu; }
    if (v < -0x7fffffffll - 1) { c->q = 1; return 0x80000000u; }
    return (uint32_t)v;
}
static inline uint32_t qadd(Cpu* c, uint32_t m, uint32_t n) { return sat32(c, (int64_t)(int32_t)m + (int32_t)n); }
static inline uint32_t qsub(Cpu* c, uint32_t m, uint32_t n) { return sat32(c, (int64_t)(int32_t)m - (int32_t)n); }
static inline uint32_t qdadd(Cpu* c, uint32_t m, uint32_t n) { return sat32(c, (int64_t)(int32_t)m + (int32_t)sat32(c, 2 * (int64_t)(int32_t)n)); }
static inline uint32_t qdsub(Cpu* c, uint32_t m, uint32_t n) { return sat32(c, (int64_t)(int32_t)m - (int32_t)sat32(c, 2 * (int64_t)(int32_t)n)); }

/* parallel add/subtract: prefix s (GE), q (signed sat), sh (signed halving), u (GE), uq, uh */
#define PAR_LANES(name, W, ST, UT, OPS, RES)                                                                \
    static inline uint32_t name(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {                                         \
        uint32_t r = 0, ge = 0; (void)ge; (void)c;                                                        \
        for (int i = 0; i < 32 / W; i++) {                                                                \
            int64_t x = (ST)(UT)(a >> (W * i)), y = (ST)(UT)(b >> (W * i)); int64_t s = OPS;              \
            (void)x; (void)y; RES;                                                                        \
        }                                                                                                 \
        return r;                                                                                         \
    }
#define PUT(v) r |= ((uint32_t)(v) & ((1u << (W * (W == 16) + 8 * (W == 8))) - 1)) << (W * i)
#define GE16(cond) if (cond) ge |= 3u << (2 * i)
#define GE8(cond) if (cond) ge |= 1u << i
static inline int64_t clamp64(int64_t v, int64_t lo, int64_t hi) { return v < lo ? lo : v > hi ? hi : v; }
#undef W
#define W 16
PAR_LANES(par_sadd16, 16, int16_t, uint16_t, x + y, { PUT(s); GE16(s >= 0); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_ssub16, 16, int16_t, uint16_t, x - y, { PUT(s); GE16(s >= 0); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_uadd16, 16, uint16_t, uint16_t, x + y, { PUT(s); GE16(s >= 0x10000); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_usub16, 16, uint16_t, uint16_t, x - y, { PUT(s); GE16(s >= 0); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_qadd16, 16, int16_t, uint16_t, clamp64(x + y, -32768, 32767), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_qsub16, 16, int16_t, uint16_t, clamp64(x - y, -32768, 32767), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uqadd16, 16, uint16_t, uint16_t, clamp64(x + y, 0, 65535), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uqsub16, 16, uint16_t, uint16_t, clamp64(x - y, 0, 65535), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_shadd16, 16, int16_t, uint16_t, (x + y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_shsub16, 16, int16_t, uint16_t, (x - y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uhadd16, 16, uint16_t, uint16_t, (x + y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uhsub16, 16, uint16_t, uint16_t, (x - y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
#undef W
#define W 8
PAR_LANES(par_sadd8, 8, int8_t, uint8_t, x + y, { PUT(s); GE8(s >= 0); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_ssub8, 8, int8_t, uint8_t, x - y, { PUT(s); GE8(s >= 0); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_uadd8, 8, uint8_t, uint8_t, x + y, { PUT(s); GE8(s >= 0x100); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_usub8, 8, uint8_t, uint8_t, x - y, { PUT(s); GE8(s >= 0); c->ge = ge; })
PAR_LANES(par_qadd8, 8, int8_t, uint8_t, clamp64(x + y, -128, 127), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_qsub8, 8, int8_t, uint8_t, clamp64(x - y, -128, 127), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uqadd8, 8, uint8_t, uint8_t, clamp64(x + y, 0, 255), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uqsub8, 8, uint8_t, uint8_t, clamp64(x - y, 0, 255), { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_shadd8, 8, int8_t, uint8_t, (x + y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_shsub8, 8, int8_t, uint8_t, (x - y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uhadd8, 8, uint8_t, uint8_t, (x + y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
PAR_LANES(par_uhsub8, 8, uint8_t, uint8_t, (x - y) >> 1, { PUT(s); })
#undef W
/* asx/sax: exchange halves of b; lane 0 = a.lo -/+ b.hi, lane 1 = a.hi +/- b.lo */
#define PAR_X(name, ST, UT, LO_OP, HI_OP, CLAMP_LO, CLAMP_HI, GEF, HALVE)                                   \
    static inline uint32_t name(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, uint32_t b) {                                         \
        int64_t al = (ST)(UT)a, ah = (ST)(UT)(a >> 16), bl = (ST)(UT)b, bh = (ST)(UT)(b >> 16);           \
        int64_t lo = al LO_OP bh, hi = ah HI_OP bl;                                                       \
        /* GEF 1: signed, GE when lane >= 0; 2: unsigned, sum lane GE when >= 0x10000, difference when >= 0 */ \
        if (GEF == 1) c->ge = ((lo >= 0) ? 3u : 0u) | ((hi >= 0) ? 0xcu : 0u);                            \
        if (GEF == 2) c->ge = ((#LO_OP[0] == '+' ? lo >= 0x10000 : lo >= 0) ? 3u : 0u) |                  \
                              ((#HI_OP[0] == '+' ? hi >= 0x10000 : hi >= 0) ? 0xcu : 0u);                 \
        if (HALVE) { lo >>= 1; hi >>= 1; }                                                                \
        lo = clamp64(lo, CLAMP_LO, CLAMP_HI); hi = clamp64(hi, CLAMP_LO, CLAMP_HI);                       \
        return ((uint32_t)lo & 0xffffu) | ((uint32_t)hi << 16);                                           \
    }
PAR_X(par_sasx, int16_t, uint16_t, -, +, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 1, 0)
PAR_X(par_ssax, int16_t, uint16_t, +, -, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 1, 0)
PAR_X(par_uasx, uint16_t, uint16_t, -, +, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 2, 0)
PAR_X(par_usax, uint16_t, uint16_t, +, -, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 2, 0)
PAR_X(par_qasx, int16_t, uint16_t, -, +, -32768, 32767, 0, 0)
PAR_X(par_qsax, int16_t, uint16_t, +, -, -32768, 32767, 0, 0)
PAR_X(par_uqasx, uint16_t, uint16_t, -, +, 0, 65535, 0, 0)
PAR_X(par_uqsax, uint16_t, uint16_t, +, -, 0, 65535, 0, 0)
PAR_X(par_shasx, int16_t, uint16_t, -, +, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 0, 1)
PAR_X(par_shsax, int16_t, uint16_t, +, -, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 0, 1)
PAR_X(par_uhasx, uint16_t, uint16_t, -, +, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 0, 1)
PAR_X(par_uhsax, uint16_t, uint16_t, +, -, INT64_MIN, INT64_MAX, 0, 1)

/* CRC32 (ARMv8): reflected polynomials 0xEDB88320 / 0x82F63B78 */
static inline uint32_t crc_bits(uint32_t crc, uint32_t v, int nbits, uint32_t poly) {
    crc ^= v;
    for (int i = 0; i < nbits; i++) crc = (crc >> 1) ^ (poly & (0u - (crc & 1)));
    return crc;
}
static inline uint32_t crc32b(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return crc_bits(a, b & 0xff, 8, 0xEDB88320u); }
static inline uint32_t crc32h(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return crc_bits(a, b & 0xffff, 16, 0xEDB88320u); }
static inline uint32_t crc32w(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return crc_bits(a, b, 32, 0xEDB88320u); }
static inline uint32_t crc32cb(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return crc_bits(a, b & 0xff, 8, 0x82F63B78u); }
static inline uint32_t crc32ch(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return crc_bits(a, b & 0xffff, 16, 0x82F63B78u); }
static inline uint32_t crc32cw(uint32_t a, uint32_t b) { return crc_bits(a, b, 32, 0x82F63B78u); }

static inline uint32_t get_cpsr(Cpu* c) {
    return ((uint32_t)c->n << 31) | ((uint32_t)c->z << 30) | ((uint32_t)c->cf << 29) | ((uint32_t)c->v << 28) |
           ((uint32_t)c->q << 27) | (c->ge << 16) | 0x10u /* user mode, ARM state */;
}
static inline void set_cpsr(Cpu* c, uint32_t v, uint32_t mask) {
    if (mask & 8) { c->n = v >> 31; c->z = (v >> 30) & 1; c->cf = (v >> 29) & 1; c->v = (v >> 28) & 1; c->q = (v >> 27) & 1; }
    if (mask & 4) c->ge = (v >> 16) & 0xf;
}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- VFP */
static inline uint32_t get_fpscr(Cpu* c) {
    return (c->fpscr & 0x0fffffffu) | ((uint32_t)c->fn << 31) | ((uint32_t)c->fz << 30) | ((uint32_t)c->fc << 29) |
           ((uint32_t)c->fv << 28);
}
static inline void set_fpscr(Cpu* c, uint32_t v) {
    c->fpscr = v & 0x0fffffffu;
    c->fn = v >> 31; c->fz = (v >> 30) & 1; c->fc = (v >> 29) & 1; c->fv = (v >> 28) & 1;
}
/* VCMP result flags: less 1000, equal 0110, greater 0010, unordered 0011 */
static inline void vfp_cmp_d(Cpu* c, double a, double b) {
    if (a != a || b != b) { c->fn = 0; c->fz = 0; c->fc = 1; c->fv = 1; }
    else if (a == b) { c->fn = 0; c->fz = 1; c->fc = 1; c->fv = 0; }
    else if (a < b) { c->fn = 1; c->fz = 0; c->fc = 0; c->fv = 0; }
    else { c->fn = 0; c->fz = 0; c->fc = 1; c->fv = 0; }
}
static inline void vfp_cmp_f(Cpu* c, float a, float b) { vfp_cmp_d(c, a, b); }
static inline float round_evenf(float x) { return nearbyintf(x); }  /* host default rounding = nearest-even */
static inline double round_even(double x) { return nearbyint(x); }

/* float -> int: ARM saturates and maps NaN to 0 (x86 would give 0x80000000) */
static inline int32_t cvt_d2s32(double x) {
    if (x != x) return 0;
    if (x >= 2147483647.0) return 2147483647;
    if (x <= -2147483648.0) return (int32_t)0x80000000;
    return (int32_t)x;
}
static inline uint32_t cvt_d2u32(double x) {
    if (x != x || x <= 0) return 0;
    if (x >= 4294967295.0) return 0xffffffffu;
    return (uint32_t)x;
}
static inline int32_t cvt_f2s32(float x) { return cvt_d2s32(x); }
static inline uint32_t cvt_f2u32(float x) { return cvt_d2u32(x); }
/* rounding variants: plain = toward zero; _r = FPSCR mode (assume nearest); _a away; _n even; _p +inf; _m -inf */
static inline double fpscr_round(Cpu* c, double x) {
    switch ((c->fpscr >> 22) & 3) {
        case 1: return ceil(x);
        case 2: return floor(x);
        case 3: return trunc(x);
        default: return nearbyint(x);
    }
}
#define VCVT_FAMILY(K, T, IN)                                                                               \
    static inline T vcvt_##K(Cpu* c, IN x) { (void)c; return cvt_##K(x); }                                \
    static inline T vcvt_##K##_r(Cpu* c, IN x) { return cvt_##K(fpscr_round(c, x)); }                      \
    static inline T vcvt_##K##_a(Cpu* c, IN x) { (void)c; return cvt_##K(round(x)); }                     \
    static inline T vcvt_##K##_n(Cpu* c, IN x) { (void)c; return cvt_##K(nearbyint(x)); }                 \
    static inline T vcvt_##K##_p(Cpu* c, IN x) { (void)c; return cvt_##K(ceil(x)); }                      \
    static inline T vcvt_##K##_m(Cpu* c, IN x) { (void)c; return cvt_##K(floor(x)); }
VCVT_FAMILY(d2s32, int32_t, double)
VCVT_FAMILY(d2u32, uint32_t, double)
VCVT_FAMILY(f2s32, int32_t, float)
VCVT_FAMILY(f2u32, uint32_t, float)

/* ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- NEON */
static inline float fmaxf_arm(float a, float b) { return (a != a || b != b) ? __builtin_nanf("") : (a > b ? a : b); }
static inline float fminf_arm(float a, float b) { return (a != a || b != b) ? __builtin_nanf("") : (a < b ? a : b); }
static inline float recip_est(float x) { return 1.0f / x; }
static inline float rsqrt_est(float x) { return 1.0f / sqrtf(x); }
static inline uint32_t recip_est_u32(uint32_t x) { (void)x; return 0xffffffffu; }

#define SAT_T(T, LO, HI)                                                                                    \
    static inline T sat_add_##T(T a, T b) { return (T)clamp64((int64_t)a + (int64_t)b, LO, HI); }          \
    static inline T sat_sub_##T(T a, T b) { return (T)clamp64((int64_t)a - (int64_t)b, LO, HI); }          \
    static inline T sat_abs_##T(T a) { return (T)clamp64(a < 0 ? -(int64_t)a : (int64_t)a, LO, HI); }      \
    static inline T sat_neg_##T(T a) { return (T)clamp64(-(int64_t)a, LO, HI); }                           \
    static inline T sat_narrow_##T(int64_t v) { return (T)clamp64(v, LO, HI); }
SAT_T(int8_t, -128, 127)
SAT_T(uint8_t, 0, 255)
SAT_T(int16_t, -32768, 32767)
SAT_T(uint16_t, 0, 65535)
SAT_T(int32_t, -2147483648ll, 2147483647ll)

static inline int64_t sat_add_int64_t(int64_t a, int64_t b) { int64_t r; return __builtin_add_overflow(a, b, &r) ? (a < 0 ? INT64_MIN : INT64_MAX) : r; }
static inline int64_t sat_sub_int64_t(int64_t a, int64_t b) { int64_t r; return __builtin_sub_overflow(a, b, &r) ? (a < 0 ? INT64_MIN : INT64_MAX) : r; }
static inline uint64_t sat_add_uint64_t(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) { uint64_t r = a + b; return r < a ? UINT64_MAX : r; }
static inline uint64_t sat_sub_uint64_t(uint64_t a, uint64_t b) { return a > b ? a - b : 0; }

/* VSHL/VRSHL by register: signed shift amount from the bottom byte of each lane of b */
#define NEON_SHL_T(T, BITS)                                                                                 \
    static inline T neon_shl_##T(T a, int8_t s8) {                                                        \
        int s = s8; /* int: negating -128 must not wrap */                                                \
        if (s >= 0) return s >= BITS ? (T)0 : (T)(a << s);                                                \
        s = -s;                                                                                           \
        if (s >= BITS) return ((T)-1 < 0 && a < 0) ? (T)-1 : (T)0;                                        \
        return (T)(a >> s);                                                                               \
    }                                                                                                     \
    static inline T neon_rshl_##T(T a, int8_t s8) {                                                       \
        int s = s8;                                                                                       \
        if (s >= 0) return neon_shl_##T(a, s8);                                                           \
        s = -s;                                                                                           \
        if (s > BITS) return 0;                                                                           \
        return (T)(((__int128)a + ((__int128)1 << (s - 1))) >> s);                                        \
    }
NEON_SHL_T(int8_t, 8)
NEON_SHL_T(uint8_t, 8)
NEON_SHL_T(int16_t, 16)
NEON_SHL_T(uint16_t, 16)
NEON_SHL_T(int32_t, 32)
NEON_SHL_T(uint32_t, 32)
NEON_SHL_T(int64_t, 64)
NEON_SHL_T(uint64_t, 64)

static inline void neon_zip(Cpu* c, int d, int m, int nbytes, int esz) {
    uint8_t a[16], b[16], o[32];
    memcpy(a, &c->vr.x[d], nbytes); memcpy(b, &c->vr.x[m], nbytes);
    int n = nbytes / esz;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { memcpy(o + (2 * i) * esz, a + i * esz, esz); memcpy(o + (2 * i + 1) * esz, b + i * esz, esz); }
    memcpy(&c->vr.x[d], o, nbytes); memcpy(&c->vr.x[m], o + nbytes, nbytes);
}
static inline void neon_uzp(Cpu* c, int d, int m, int nbytes, int esz) {
    uint8_t in[32], o[32];
    memcpy(in, &c->vr.x[d], nbytes); memcpy(in + nbytes, &c->vr.x[m], nbytes);
    int n = nbytes / esz;
    for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) { memcpy(o + i * esz, in + (2 * i) * esz, esz); memcpy(o + nbytes + i * esz, in + (2 * i + 1) * esz, esz); }
    memcpy(&c->vr.x[d], o, nbytes); memcpy(&c->vr.x[m], o + nbytes, nbytes);
}
static inline void neon_trn(Cpu* c, int d, int m, int nbytes, int esz) {
    uint8_t a[16], b[16];
    memcpy(a, &c->vr.x[d], nbytes); memcpy(b, &c->vr.x[m], nbytes);
    int n = nbytes / esz;
    for (int i = 0; i + 1 < n; i += 2) {
        uint8_t t[8];
        memcpy(t, a + (i + 1) * esz, esz); memcpy(a + (i + 1) * esz, b + i * esz, esz); memcpy(b + i * esz, t, esz);
    }
    memcpy(&c->vr.x[d], a, nbytes); memcpy(&c->vr.x[m], b, nbytes);
}
static inline void neon_tbl(Cpu* c, int d, int t0, int nt, int idx, int ext) {
    uint8_t tbl[32], ix[8], out[8];
    for (int i = 0; i < nt; i++) memcpy(tbl + 8 * i, &c->vr.x[(t0 + i) & 31], 8);
    memcpy(ix, &c->vr.x[idx], 8); memcpy(out, &c->vr.x[d], 8);
    for (int i = 0; i < 8; i++) out[i] = ix[i] < 8 * nt ? tbl[ix[i]] : (ext ? out[i] : 0);
    memcpy(&c->vr.x[d], out, 8);
}
/* VLDn/VSTn multiple structures: members m at D(d + m*inc + r), elements interleaved in memory */
static inline void neon_ldst_multi(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, int d, int n, int inc, int regs, int esz, int load) {
    int per = 8 / esz;
    for (int r = 0; r < regs; r++)
        for (int e = 0; e < per; e++)
            for (int m = 0; m < n; m++) {
                uint8_t* reg = (uint8_t*)&c->vr.x[(d + m * inc + r) & 31] + e * esz;
                if (load) memcpy(reg, GPTR(a), esz); else memcpy(GPTR(a), reg, esz);
                a += esz;
            }
}
static inline void neon_ldst_lane(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, int d, int n, int inc, int esz, int idx, int load) {
    for (int m = 0; m < n; m++) {
        uint8_t* reg = (uint8_t*)&c->vr.x[(d + m * inc) & 31] + idx * esz;
        if (load) memcpy(reg, GPTR(a), esz); else memcpy(GPTR(a), reg, esz);
        a += esz;
    }
}
static inline void neon_ld_all(Cpu* c, uint32_t a, int d, int n, int inc, int esz, int regs) {
    for (int m = 0; m < n; m++) {
        uint8_t v[8];
        memcpy(v, GPTR(a), esz);
        a += esz;
        for (int r = 0; r < regs; r++) {
            uint8_t* reg = (uint8_t*)&c->vr.x[(d + m * inc + r) & 31];
            for (int e = 0; e < 8 / esz; e++) memcpy(reg + e * esz, v, esz);
        }
    }
}

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif
```

```cpp
// TMSRecomp launcher (launcher.exe next to tms.exe): edits settings.ini, manages mods, updates from GitHub releases
// and starts the game. Drawn with Direct2D / DirectWrite (Windows components, no other dependency). Only keys this
// window knows are rewritten; comments and any other lines in settings.ini are kept.
// Linux: the same pages through linux_shim.h (SDL3 window, cairo / pango drawing); its own window loop, setup runner
// and update check are below, next to the Windows versions.
#ifdef _WIN32
#include <windows.h>
#include <d2d1.h>
#include <dwmapi.h>
#include <dwrite_1.h>
#include <shellapi.h>
#include <shlobj.h>

#include <windowsx.h>
#include <commdlg.h>
#else
#include "linux_shim.h"

#include <locale>
#include <fcntl.h>

extern char** environ;
#endif

// ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ settings.ini
static fs::path g_dir, g_ini, g_data;
static std::vector<std::string> g_lines;
static bool g_dirty = false;

static std::string trim(std::string s) {
    s.erase(0, s.find_first_not_of(" \t\r"));
    s.erase(s.find_last_not_of(" \t\r") + 1);
    return s;
}

// The key of an uncommented "key = value" line (lower case, as tms.exe upper-cases it anyway), else "".
static std::string key_of(const std::string& line) {
    std::string l = line.substr(0, line.find_first_of(";#"));
    size_t eq = l.find('=');
    if (eq == std::string::npos) return "";
    std::string k = trim(l.substr(0, eq));
    std::transform(k.begin(), k.end(), k.begin(), ::tolower);
    return k;
}

static std::string get(const char* k, const char* def) {
    for (auto& l : g_lines)
        if (key_of(l) == k) {
            std::string v = trim(l.substr(0, l.find_first_of(";#")).substr(l.find('=') + 1));
            return v.empty() ? def : v;
        }
    return def;
}

static void set(const char* k, const std::string& v) {
    g_dirty = true;
    for (auto& l : g_lines)
        if (key_of(l) == k) {
            l = std::string(k) + " = " + v;
            return;
        }
    if (!v.empty()) g_lines.push_back(std::string(k) + " = " + v);
}

// ANSI like tms.exe's getenv (ponytail: non-ASCII data paths need the wide-char API on both sides).
#ifdef _WIN32
static std::wstring wide(const std::string& s) {
    std::wstring w(MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, s.c_str(), -1, nullptr, 0), 0);
    MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, s.c_str(), -1, w.data(), (int)w.size());
    w.pop_back();
    return w;
}
static std::string narrow(const std::wstring& w) {
    std::string s(WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, w.c_str(), -1, nullptr, 0, nullptr, nullptr), 0);
    WideCharToMultiByte(CP_ACP, 0, w.c_str(), -1, s.data(), (int)s.size(), nullptr, nullptr);
    s.pop_back();
    return s;
}
#else
static std::wstring wide(const std::string& s) { return draw::wide(s); }  // Linux: UTF-8 everywhere
static std::string narrow(const std::wstring& w) { return draw::utf8(w); }
#endif

static bool is_data(const fs::path& p) {
    std::error_code ec;
    return fs::exists(p / "link" / "image.bin", ec) && fs::exists(p / "romfs", ec);
}

// The data folder tms.exe will use: ini "data", else the folder above the build folder (tms.exe's order).
static void find_data() {
    std::string d = get("data", "");
    g_data = !d.empty() ? fs::path(wide(d)) : is_data(g_dir.parent_path()) ? g_dir.parent_path() : fs::path();
}

static void load() {
    if (!fs::exists(g_ini)) std::ofstream(g_ini) << k_default_settings;
    g_lines.clear();
    std::ifstream f(g_ini);
    for (std::string l; std::getline(f, l);) g_lines.push_back(l);
    find_data();
}

static bool save() {
    std::ofstream f(g_ini);
    for (auto& l : g_lines) f << l << "\n";
    if (f) g_dirty = false;
    return (bool)f;
}
```
